messages:
alex: heads-up — saw a weird throughput drop on H100 when we enabled the new kernel-selection heuristics on main. baseline (old heur) was ~850k tokens/s, after change we're seeing ~600k tokens/s on the same load. likely kernel fallback on certain attention shapes.
maria: ouch. any profile traces?
alex: pasted quick perf dump from the trace: ```
# perf-summary
model: llama-2-13b; seq=2048; batch-seqs=8; kv-growth=2048
kernel_choice: optimized_attention_nvgpu -> fallback_matmul
time: total=1.66s tokens=1.4M throughput=843k tok/s (old)
         total=2.33s tokens=1.4M throughput=600k tok/s (new)
hotspots:
  - fallback_matmul (40% of time)
  - kv-copy (12% of time, grows with seq)
  - cuda_launch_overhead (7%)
```
jordan: looks like the heuristic picked an attention kernel that doesn't scale well for >1024 seq lengths on H100. fallback_matmul is generic but not quant-optimized. did kernel selector change the shape threshold?
alex: yes — selector lowered the cutoff to prefer the new tiled kernel for smaller shapes, but for some combinations it forces a path that triggers a fallback for large seqs. Also noticed KV cache copies are done per-request for that path.
devon: KV behavior matters here. if we let batches accumulate with mixed seq lengths we blow cache footprint and cause more host<->device churn. we should factor kv_growth into token budget.
maria: agreed. proposal: add per-GPU defaults for two knobs: max_batch_seqs (max number of sequences per batch) and max_tokens_per_batch (sum of seq lengths in batch). use conservative defaults that avoid kernel fallback and leave 20-30% GPU mem headroom for KV.
jordan: propose numbers after hands-on tuning (rough estimates):
- T4: max_batch_seqs=24, max_tokens_per_batch=8k
- L4: max_batch_seqs=32, max_tokens_per_batch=12k
- A10: max_batch_seqs=48, max_tokens_per_batch=20k
- A100: max_batch_seqs=96, max_tokens_per_batch=48k
- H100: max_batch_seqs=128, max_tokens_per_batch=96k
these are conservative; aim for token_budget_target=0.7 (70% of estimated usable memory).
alex: I like it. add an override map keyed by model_seq (e.g., for seq<=512 allow higher batch counts) so short contexts still get packed.
devon: also adjust queue policy: prefer latency-slo-first for interactive tier, but for batch tier use aggressive fill-within-50ms-window. we should implement a small penalty in the scheduler for batches that would trigger the slow kernel (if kernel selector can predict fallback).
maria: practical steps —
1) rollout per-gpu defaults to staging (config flag: continuous_batching.per_gpu_limits)
2) enable perf-metrics tag when kernel fallback happens (perf-bucket = "kernel_fallback")
3) run 24h canary with mixed seq-length trace and compare p99 lat and throughput
4) iterate on numbers if p99 > latency_slo or throughput regresses >5%
alex: example config snippet I tested locally: ```json
{
  "continuous_batching": {
    "per_gpu_limits": {
      "T4": {"max_batch_seqs": 24, "max_tokens_per_batch": 8000},
      "L4": {"max_batch_seqs": 32, "max_tokens_per_batch": 12000},
      "A10": {"max_batch_seqs": 48, "max_tokens_per_batch": 20000},
      "A100": {"max_batch_seqs": 96, "max_tokens_per_batch": 48000},
      "H100": {"max_batch_seqs": 128, "max_tokens_per_batch": 96000}
    },
    "token_budget_target": 0.7,
    "queue_policy": {"interactive_window_ms": 20, "batch_window_ms": 50}
  }
}
```
maria: can you also add a metric: gauge kernel_fallback_rate per gpu_type + model_name? we need to see if any model still triggers it often.
devon: yep will add a metric and a trace log event. also will instrument kv_copy_bytes and kv_copy_time to see if we can optimize the copy path instead of lowering batch limits.
jordan: FYI I ran a quick canary with the above H100 limits and saw throughput recover to ~820k tok/s and p99 latency improved 18%. memory headroom stayed ~25%. leaving the patch on staging now.
alex: great. next: decide whether to change kernel selector thresholds upstream or keep this as a compensating per-gpu constraint. my vote: short-term per-gpu limits, long-term improve selector to avoid forced fallback for common shapes.
maria: +1. also add a small experiment: on H100 allow one 'speculative' larger batch once every N seconds to see if the kernel path changes (maybe a transient allocation avoids fallback). record results.
devon: tracking ticket: INF-3372, I'll attach perf traces and config diff. cc @sre-bot to schedule canary. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: Canary scheduled: INF-3372 on staging cluster (h100-pool) for 12h. alerts: p99_latency > 1.5x baseline OR throughput drop >8% will rollback.
alex: thanks. I'll follow up after 12h with a short results summary and updated recommended defaults.
maria: nice work team, sounds like a solid plan. :rocket:
